text:
**Short answer:** For most weekend campers, the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** is the best pick. It weighs 8.3 lb, stores 288 Wh, and covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP for several nights. If you want more output or plan to run a fridge, step up to a 1,000 Wh unit.

## Recommendations by trip type

**Weekend camping, phones, lights, CPAP: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249)**
PowerStationGearLab names this its best overall camping pick: 288 Wh LiFePO4, about 8.3 lb, and 300 W AC output. It also notes that Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
[Search Amazon for Jackery Explorer 300 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+300+Plus)

**Best value: EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269–299)**
Same 286 Wh capacity as the Jackery, but with a 600 W inverter (double the Jackery's) and expandability to 572 Wh. It weighs about 9.9 lb. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
[Search Amazon for EcoFlow River 3 Plus](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EcoFlow+River+3+Plus)

**Budget: Bluetti EB3A (~$179)**
268 Wh LiFePO4 with a 600 W inverter. The app is basic and the build is less polished, but it's a solid entry point. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
[Search Amazon for Bluetti EB3A](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Bluetti+EB3A)

**Longer trips, small fridge, or power tools: Jackery Explorer 1000 V2 (~$799 list)**
1,070 Wh and 1,500 W, but about 23.8 lb. TechRadar lists it as its best-for-camping pick. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
[Search Amazon for Jackery Explorer 1000 V2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+1000+V2)

**Mid-size alternative: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (under $530 on sale)**
OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. It measured 890 Wh and 25.2 lb, and it's noisier than the Jackery units. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
[Search Amazon for Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C1000+Gen+2)

**Extended off-grid: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (~$900 on Amazon)**
OutdoorGearLab's top pick for multi-day off-grid trips. It measured 1,710 Wh usable and weighs 39 lb. It can't run a space heater for long, and it has no battery expansion. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
[Search Amazon for Jackery Explorer 2000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+2000+v2)

**Bluetti AC180 (listed at $499)**
1,152 Wh, 1,800 W continuous, 500 W solar input, about 16 kg, with a 5-year warranty. This review is from a site that earns a commission on sales. The page lists a discount code, but checkout determines the final price. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
[Buy at Dealectric's BLUETTI link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

## How to choose
- **Capacity:** Add up your device draws. Phones use about 10 Wh per charge, and a CPAP uses 30–60 Wh per night. Turn off the CPAP humidifier to roughly triple its battery life. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Weight:** If you carry it far from the car, stay under about 10 lb.
- **Fridge:** A 12V fridge at around 40–50 W needs roughly 1,000 Wh or more for a full day.

Prices and availability change, and the search links above are not verified product listings. Check the current price before you buy.
